reasons.claim: One eligible species is recorded within 250 m. Alectoria sarmentosa (VU, lichen) is site-bound and forest-associated, with felling-relevant threats (lack of continuity forest, lack of large or old trees, changed stand structure). Its record is 100 m from the polygon edge, dated 2017, with 5 m uncertainty.

Hydnellum ferrugineum (NT, fungus, forest-associated, felling-relevant) has 5 records within 250 m, at 79–159 m, including several from 2025. As an NT species it is supporting evidence only and does not count as eligible. The count of site-bound forest NT species within 250 m is 1, below the threshold of 3.
Completed felling covers 1.9% of the polygon (0.151 ha, a 2003 felling), so the site is not already felled.
Effort is adequate (214 records within 1000 m vs county median 128.5). Within 250 m there are 30 records on 7 days, so the area has been recorded.

uncertainties: The Alectoria sarmentosa record is from 2017 and lies outside the polygon, so it does not show current occupancy of the felling site.
2 near-site records were dropped for coordinate uncertainty, and the effort tool also lists 2 coarse records excluded within 250 m.
A Trifolium spadiceum (NT) record lies at 0 m. It is not forest-associated according to the tool and does not affect priority.
not_established: That Alectoria sarmentosa or Hydnellum ferrugineum occupies the polygon today.
Stand age or condition, because no tool describes it.
Whether the felling is legal or appropriate.
That species not recorded are absent.
next_action: Have an ecologist review the site. Check where the Alectoria sarmentosa record and the Hydnellum ferrugineum records sit relative to the polygon boundary and the stand, and consider a field check before felling begins.
